final_recommendation: The room converged on a multi-layered underwriting framework: Big Four SOX 404(b) audits as placement gates, 5-day certification windows with retroactive cancellation on breach, sector-wide repricing on day-one contagion signals (15-20% premium lift), carved-out counsel-defense reserves (30-month officers' defense + separate E&O self-defense tail), and real-time treaty reinsurer notification on audit flags. The framework operationalizes contagion speed (15-day cascade vs. 60-day baseline) and creates priced accumulation triggers, but relies on real-time deposit-velocity signals the room acknowledged may not exist yet.
minority_objections: ai_agent_analyst raised that customer-run signals hit before audit flags, meaning repricing may be 'three days too late' without real-time deposit-velocity data
emerging_risk_lead questioned whether the room was tracking customer/creditor phone calls (24-hour contagion) vs. just cert failures
dando_specialist warned the retroactive cancellation framework shifts exposure to the tail rather than eliminating it
key_conflicts: Whether the 5-day cert window creates systemic accumulation risk during sector shocks (reinsurance_manager vs. financial_lines_underwriter)
Whether CFO self-certification is adequate or requires independent Big Four validation (eo_specialist, claims_counsel vs. initial proposal)
Whether contagion window is 60 days (portfolio count) or 15-20 days (cascade collapse) — resolved in favor of 15-day model
Whether to reserve for officers' defense and E&O self-defense separately or together — resolved with two-bucket approach
key_concessions: financial_lines_underwriter conceded Big Four audit requirement as placement gate after five specialists flagged self-attestation gap
reinsurance_manager conceded need to notify treaty panel day-one of audit flag (not cancellation) after ai_agent_analyst showed 15-day cascade
claims_counsel conceded separate 24-month E&O self-defense reserve after eo_specialist identified self-referential liability chain
financial_lines_underwriter carved out $2M peer-contagion sublimit after dando_specialist showed Client B coverage gap risk
red_lines: No placement without Big Four SOX 404(b) control assessment (eo_specialist, reinsurance_manager, claims_counsel)
Retroactive cancellation to discovery date on material weakness — non-negotiable (financial_lines_underwriter)
Day-one treaty reinsurer notification on audit flags — no waiting for cancellation (reinsurance_manager)
Separate E&O self-defense reserve — cannot be conflated with officers' defense tail (eo_specialist, claims_counsel)
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Real-time deposit-velocity monitoring: ai_agent_analyst identified that customer-run signals precede audit flags by days, but the room has no operational data feed for this
Social media contagion speed: emerging_risk_lead noted board-level departures hit Twitter before compliance inboxes, but no monitoring mechanism was operationalized
Auditor-change seam: eo_specialist flagged scope reductions and auditor swaps as control-gap hiding places, but no re-audit trigger was finalized
Self-referential E&O endpoint: dando_specialist warned the E&O self-defense tail 'doesn't have a natural endpoint' if settlements get clawed back iteratively
downstream_risk_variables: Big Four material weakness flag as day-one repricing trigger (15-20% premium lift on peer cohort)
15-day contagion cascade window (vs. 60-day baseline) as reinsurance accumulation trigger
Customer-run signal velocity (24-hour phone-call contagion) as leading indicator, though not yet operationalized
Retroactive cancellation to discovery date as claims-tail containment mechanism
Carved-out $2M peer-contagion sublimit for forced cross-policy officer defense
Separate 30-month officers' defense reserve and non-eroding E&O self-defense reserve
Additional 12-18 month clawback tail reserve triggered only on AT1 bondholder motion
uncertainty_notes: The framework assumes real-time deposit-velocity and social-media monitoring that the room acknowledged may not exist operationally ('are we pulling SEC filings in real-time, or do we still wait for the client's rider?'). The 15-day cascade model is theoretically sound but untested in live underwriting. The E&O self-defense tail's endpoint remains undefined if clawback motions iterate. The sector-repricing mechanism depends on detecting customer-run signals 'in hour 12' — no participant confirmed this data feed is live.
